north-shore-auditorium.sourceEn: gooood | North Shore Auditorium, Qinhuangdao / Vector Architects
notesEn: Three concave exterior walls recede from the neighboring buildings, while the raised ground floor lets people cross the plaza beneath the building. In section, the daylit music hall sits above a circular meditation room. Viewed from below, the sunken stage resembles a suspended disc. Nine brass apertures along the seating edge carry the sound of performances into the room. Gaps around the stage and at the base of the walls admit diffuse light. Operable vents at the base provide ventilation. When the circular ETFE cushion roof rises, the hall becomes an open-air theater.

notesEn: The design begins in section. The long north–south axis connects the spaces directly, while the short axis defines how each space relates to the sea. Stepped seating raises the sightlines at the back of the reading room. Above its 20-metre seaward window, a steel truss supports the roof, and translucent glass blocks on either side change with the light. On the east facade, a 1.2-metre recess and a horizontal beam screen direct morning sunlight. Circular roof ducts provide ventilation and admit afternoon light. The meditation room has a concave roof that lowers the ceiling, with 30-centimetre slots at its east and west ends admitting light at dawn and dusk.

boa-nova-tea-house.sourceEn: Archiposition | Boa Nova Tea House: Between Rocks and Waves
notesEn: The irregular plan follows the rocky slope, and in section the gently pitched roofs extend the line of the terrain. Steps and landings lead to an entrance beneath low eaves. A narrow horizontal window first frames the horizon. Downstairs, full-height glazing brings the view down to the rocks and waves nearby. Gaps between the staggered roofs admit daylight. Deep eaves shelter the north terrace, while the south tea room’s sill height is set for seated views.

songyang-three-temple-cultural-center.sourceEn: Archiposition | Wenli District Conservation and Renewal / Jiakun Architects
notesEn: The old buildings were assigned different levels of protection. Later additions were cleared to open public space in front of the two temples and reconnect alleys to surrounding neighborhoods. A new single-storey weathering-steel covered walkway avoids mature trees and retained buildings. Narrow stretches connect the old houses, while wider sections accommodate a bookstore, cafés and other uses. The roof stays below the historic eaves, and the foundations avoid deep excavation. Qingyun Road connects the temples, courtyards and new spaces into a neighborhood people can walk through.

notesEn: Komaeyu occupies the ground floor of a residential building. The renovation connects the former street-front pub and the baths behind it through a reception counter, bar and tiled Mount Fuji wall. The neighboring vacant lot provides a place to sit after bathing. Three sizes of green tiles from Tajimi share aligned joints, making the variation subtle and connecting the interior palette with the surrounding greenery.

notesEn: The renovation kept the existing bathing areas at their original size and reused redundant service rooms for new uses, including a sauna, an open-air cold bath and a bar. A 2.25-metre partition between the two bathing areas sets the material datum below the exposed concrete structure. At the entrance it drops to 1.15 metres, aligning with the bar counter where visitors can meet.

notesEn: After a lightning fire, the main building was rebuilt on the surviving substructure with a lightweight timber frame. Clerestories between the staggered roofs bring light into the shared areas. The raised timber ceiling and translucent surfaces are visible beside the shoe lockers and children’s play area. Deep eaves shelter the transition outdoors, while seating, dining and overnight accommodation support the onsen’s community role.

notesEn: The baths are set halfway into the slope, with turf-covered roofs continuing the ground above. Inside, layered local stone ties together the finishes and walls, while massive blocks define bathing spaces of different sizes. Slits between the roof slabs cast light onto stone and water. The route alternates between dim, low passages, open pools and smaller rooms for lingering.
